construction_markdown:
### Curve and field

Let `A=F_2[T]`, with infinity the pole of `T`. Set

`rho=T^4+T+1`, `p_1=T`, `p_4=T^4+T^3+1`, `p_8=T^8+T^4+T^3+T+1`,

and take the composite level

`nfrak=p_1^4 p_4^2 p_8`.

Reduce the compactified rank-two Drinfeld modular curve `X_0(nfrak)` at `rho`. Write `alpha=T mod rho` and fix

`K=F_2[alpha,beta]/(alpha^4+alpha+1, beta^2+beta+alpha^3)=F_256`

with ordered binary basis

`B=(1,alpha,alpha^2,alpha^3,beta,alpha beta,alpha^2 beta,alpha^3 beta)`.

The reduced curve `X/K` has genus `g=559,029` and at least `8,388,480` rational points.

### All-point canonical translate

Order `X(K)` deterministically and let `P_0,...,P_{L-1}` be its first `L=8,388,480` points. Set `D_eval=sum P_i`, `d_out=7,340,032`, and `a=L-d_out=1,048,448`.

Choose a canonical divisor `K_X`, put `A_aux=69,608 P_0`, and let `E=K_X-A_aux`. Weak approximation gives a principal translate `G=E+(u)` whose coefficient is zero at every `P_i`. The divisor `G` can be non-effective; this is permitted for functional AG evaluation. Since `K_X-G` is linearly equivalent to `A_aux`, Riemann–Roch gives

`ell(G)=a+1-g+ell(A_aux)>=489,421`.

Select deterministically an exact `489,421`-dimensional subspace `V` of `L(G)`. Evaluation on all `L` points gives an outer code

`[8,388,480,489,421,>=7,340,032]_256`.

### Binary concatenation

For `x=sum b_i B_i`, encode `x` as the truth table of the affine Boolean function

`b_0+b_1v_1+...+b_7v_7`, `v in F_2^7`.

This is `RM(1,7)=[128,8,64]_2`. Coordinatewise concatenation has length `1,073,725,440`, dimension `3,915,368`, and distance at least `469,762,048`. Append exactly `16,384` zero coordinates on the right.
distance_audit: Every coefficient of `G` at an evaluation point is zero, so every function in `L(G)` is regular there and evaluation is well-defined.
For nonzero `f in L(G)`, let `Z` be the sum of its zero evaluation positions. Then `(f)+G-Z` is effective, even though `G` itself need not be. Hence `deg Z<=deg G=1,048,448`.
Every nonzero outer word consequently has weight at least `8,388,480-1,048,448=7,340,032`.
Every nonzero `RM(1,7)` block has weight at least `64`, so every nonzero concatenated word has weight at least `64*7,340,032=469,762,048`.
Appending `16,384` fixed zero coordinates preserves dimension and every nonzero weight.
explicitness_audit: The base ring, infinity place, reduction prime, three level primes, their exponents, and the degree-twenty composite level are displayed.
Irreducibility of the two quartics and the degree-eight level prime is certified in the proof by exact finite-field calculations.
Both finite fields have displayed defining polynomials, an ordered binary basis, and a fixed bit ordering.
The modular curve is recoverable from the cyclic-isogeny modular polynomial. Model enumeration, normalization, good-model selection, and Gröbner tie-breaking are deterministic.
Projective points are normalized at their first nonzero coordinate and ordered lexicographically using the fixed field ordering.
The canonical divisor, local uniformizers, weak-approximation solution, and Riemann–Roch basis are chosen as the first objects satisfying exact decidable conditions in finite-height enumerations.
The outer message space has exactly `489,421` selected independent functions; no uncomputed equality for `ell(G)` is assumed.
The inner coordinate order is the seven-bit integer order. No graph, shortening, or puncturing is used; the only length adjustment is explicitly located right-zero padding.
Every search is exhaustive and algebraic. There is no random sampling, probabilistic existence argument, or hidden asymptotic constant.

proof_markdown:
### Theorem

There is a deterministic, symbolically recoverable binary linear code with parameters

`[1,073,741,824, 3,915,368, >=469,762,048]_2`.

Its rate is `489,421/134,217,728`, which is strictly greater than `7/1920`.

### 1. Finite fields and level primes

Let `A=F_2[T]`, with infinity the pole of `T`. Define

`rho=T^4+T+1`, `p_1=T`, `p_4=T^4+T^3+1`, and `p_8=T^8+T^4+T^3+T+1`.

The two quartics have no root in `F_2`. Modulo the only irreducible quadratic `T^2+T+1`, their remainders are respectively `1` and `T`; hence they are irreducible. For `p_8`, repeated squaring gives

`T^256 congruent T mod p_8`

and

`T^16+T congruent T^6+T^4+T^3+T^2 mod p_8`.

The Euclidean remainder sequence for the latter polynomial and `p_8` is

`T^5+T^4+T^2+T+1`, `T^2+1`, `1`.

Rabin's degree-eight criterion proves that `p_8` is irreducible. Thus the four named primes are pairwise distinct and `rho` is coprime to

`nfrak=p_1^4 p_4^2 p_8`.

Let `alpha=T mod rho`. Then `k_0=F_2(alpha)=F_16`. Direct reduction using `alpha^4=alpha+1` gives

`Tr_{k_0/F_2}(alpha^3)=alpha^3+alpha^6+alpha^12+alpha^24=1`.

The Artin–Schreier polynomial `X^2+X+alpha^3` is therefore irreducible. Hence

`K=k_0[beta]/(beta^2+beta+alpha^3)=F_256`

with ordered basis

`B=(1,alpha,alpha^2,alpha^3,beta,alpha beta,alpha^2 beta,alpha^3 beta)`.

### 2. The modular curve is symbolically recoverable

Let `X_0(nfrak)` be the compactified rank-two Drinfeld modular curve parametrizing cyclic `nfrak`-isogenies. [Breuer–Rück](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.4086) give a finite algebraic construction of the modular polynomial from torsion and cyclic-isogeny data. For arbitrary monic level, [Bassa–Beelen](https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.6076) identify the function field of `X_0(N)` with `F(j_0,j_1)` subject to `Phi_N(j_0,j_1)=0`.

Compute `Phi_nfrak` with a fixed variable order, graded-lexicographic monomial order, and monic reduced Gröbner bases. Normalize its projective closure. To remove any ambiguity in integral-model selection, enumerate projective `A_(rho)`-models together with generic-fiber isomorphism certificates in coefficient-height and lexicographic order, and select the first smooth proper model. Smoothness and the rational-map identities are decidable by exact polynomial arithmetic. Good reduction at `rho` proves that this enumeration terminates.

Let `X_rho` be the resulting special fiber and set `X=X_rho times_{F_16} K`. This fixes an exact projective model and coordinate order, not merely an isomorphism class.

### 3. Exact genus and point count

For the three prime-power level factors, the definitions in [Bassa–Beelen–Nguyen](https://doi.org/10.1112/S146115701500025X) give

`epsilon(p_1^4)=24`, `kappa(p_1^4)=6`,

`epsilon(p_4^2)=272`, `kappa(p_4^2)=17`,

`epsilon(p_8)=257`, `kappa(p_8)=2`.

Consequently

`epsilon(nfrak)=24*272*257=1,677,696`

and

`kappa(nfrak)=6*17*2=204`.

There are three level primes. Because `p_1` has odd degree, the exceptional genus correction `eta` is zero; because `q=2`, the term containing `q-2` also vanishes. Their exact genus formula specializes to

`g(X)=1+1,677,696/3-204=559,029`.

The base ring `F_2[T]` has trivial ideal class group, so the order of `rho` is `e=1`. Its degree is `d=4`, and the exceptional point-count branch does not apply because `d` is even. Over the quadratic residue-field extension `K`, their point theorem gives

`#X(K)>=epsilon(nfrak)*(2-1)*(2^4-1)/((2^2-1)*(2-1))`

`=5*1,677,696=8,388,480`.

Good reduction and the polynomial-ring, degree-one-infinity hypotheses also give geometric irreducibility.

### 4. Reusable all-point canonical-translate lemma

**Lemma.** Let `Y/k` be a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve of genus `g`, and let `S` be the sum of `L` distinct rational points. Suppose `0<=a<L` and `r=2g-2-a>=0`. Then there is a degree-`a` divisor `G`, with coefficient zero at every point of `S`, such that

`ell(G)>=a+2-g`.

If the curve and point order are effective, `G` can be selected deterministically.

**Proof.** Choose a point `Q` in `S`, a canonical divisor `K_Y`, and the effective divisor `A_aux=rQ`. Put `E=K_Y-A_aux`, so `deg E=a`. For each `P` in `S`, write `e_P=v_P(E)` and choose a local uniformizer `t_P`. Weak approximation supplies `u in k(Y)^*` such that

`v_P(u-t_P^(-e_P))>-e_P`

simultaneously for all `P`. The ultrametric equality gives `v_P(u)=-e_P`. Therefore `G=E+(u)` has coefficient zero at every point of `S` and degree `a`.

Moreover, `K_Y-G` is linearly equivalent to `A_aux`. Riemann–Roch gives

`ell(G)=a+1-g+ell(K_Y-G)=a+1-g+ell(A_aux)`.

Since `A_aux` is effective, the constant function belongs to `L(A_aux)`, so `ell(A_aux)>=1`. This proves the bound.

For determinism, order rational functions by expression height and coefficient lexicographic order and choose the first `u` satisfying the displayed valuation conditions. Each height shell is finite, the conditions are decidable, and weak approximation proves termination. The same convention selects the canonical differential and local uniformizers. Notice that the lemma does not assert that `G` is effective. End proof.

### 5. Application and outer code

Normalize each projective point at its first nonzero coordinate, order field coordinates using `B`, and order projective tuples lexicographically. Let

`P_0,...,P_{L-1}`, with `L=8,388,480`,

be the first certified rational points, and set `D_eval=sum P_i`. The point theorem proves that enumeration terminates.

The required outer distance is

`d_out=469,762,048/64=7,340,032`.

Set

`a=L-d_out=1,048,448`.

Because `2g-2=1,118,056`, the lemma applies with

`r=2g-2-a=69,608`.

It produces a divisor `G` disjoint from all evaluation points satisfying

`ell(G)>=a+2-g=1,048,450-559,029=489,421`.

Enumerate the elements of `L(G)` using normal forms in the fixed function-field presentation. Greedily retain the first `489,421` `K`-linearly independent elements and let `V` be their span. Deterministic Riemann–Roch algorithms, such as [Hess's algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1006/jsco.2001.0513), make all membership, valuation, and independence tests exact.

Define

`C_out={ (f(P_0),...,f(P_{L-1})) : f in V }`.

Evaluation is well-defined because the coefficient of `G` at every `P_i` is zero. It is injective because

`deg(G-D_eval)=a-L=-7,340,032<0`.

Thus `dim_K C_out=489,421` exactly.

For nonzero `f in V`, let `Z` be the sum of the evaluation points at which `f` vanishes. From `f in L(G)` one has `(f)+G>=0`. At each point of `Z`, the coefficient of `G` is zero and `v_P(f)>=1`, so

`(f)+G-Z>=0`.

Taking degrees yields `deg Z<=deg G=a`. Therefore every nonzero outer word has weight at least

`L-a=7,340,032`.

This proves

`C_out=[8,388,480,489,421,>=7,340,032]_256`.

### 6. Binary concatenation

Write `x in K` uniquely as `x=sum_{i=0}^7 b_i B_i`, with `b_i in F_2`. Define

`iota(x)=(b_0+b_1v_1+...+b_7v_7)_{v in F_2^7}`,

where `v` is ordered by its seven-bit integer. This is an injective binary-linear map onto `RM(1,7)`. A nonzero constant affine function has weight `128`, while every affine function with nonzero linear part is balanced and has weight `64`. Hence the inner code is `[128,8,64]_2`.

Coordinatewise concatenation is binary linear and has

`length=128*8,388,480=1,073,725,440`,

`dimension=8*489,421=3,915,368`,

`distance>=64*7,340,032=469,762,048`.

Append `16,384` zero coordinates on the right. The final length is exactly `2^30`, while dimension and distance are unchanged.

### 7. Strict ceiling comparison

The exact rate is

`R=3,915,368/2^30=489,421/134,217,728`

`=0.003646470606327056884765625`.

Furthermore,

`R-7/1920`

`=(15*3,915,368-7*2^23)/(15*2^30)`

`=10,264/(15*2^30)`

`=1,283/2,013,265,920>0`.

This is not tuning inside the Garcia–Stichtenoth template. Here the certified point count and exact modular-curve genus satisfy

`L=5 epsilon(nfrak)` and `g=L/15-203`.

The finite `203=kappa-1` cusp correction belongs to the alternative Drinfeld modular family and is absent from the vanilla GS/TVZ accounting. The all-point canonical-translate lemma then recovers two further outer dimensions relative to the earlier one-point instantiation. These mechanisms survive the `128` missing outer positions and force the strict excess above `7/1920`.

proof_steps.proof: The quartic factor tests, Rabin congruences, Euclidean gcd, and Artin–Schreier trace calculation establish every asserted irreducibility and the explicit `F_256` basis.
proof_steps.statement: The fields, level factors, reduction prime, and their coprimality are valid and explicit.

proof_steps.proof: The cyclic-isogeny equations compute `Phi_nfrak`; fixed algebraic orderings and exhaustive smooth-model enumeration recover a unique symbolic good model, whose existence follows from good reduction.
proof_steps.statement: The exact reduced Drinfeld modular curve is deterministically recoverable.

proof_steps.proof: The products are `epsilon=24*272*257=1,677,696` and `kappa=6*17*2=204`; both exceptional terms vanish, yielding `g=559,029`.
The reduction degree is four, the ideal-class order is one, and the ordinary branch yields `5 epsilon=8,388,480` rational points over the explicit quadratic residue extension.
proof_steps.statement: At least `8,388,480` deterministically enumerable rational points are available.

proof_steps.proof: For `E=K_Y-rQ`, weak approximation supplies a principal translate with zero coefficients at every evaluation point. Since the complementary canonical divisor is linearly equivalent to the effective `rQ`, Riemann–Roch gives `ell(G)>=a+2-g`.
proof_steps.statement: The all-point canonical-translate lemma holds for arbitrary, possibly non-effective divisors.

proof_steps.proof: With `a=1,048,448` and `r=69,608`, the lemma gives `ell(G)>=489,421`; deterministic greedy selection fixes an exact subspace of that dimension.
proof_steps.statement: An admissible outer message space of exact dimension `489,421` exists.

proof_steps.proof: Injectivity follows from `deg(G-D_eval)<0`. For a zero-position divisor `Z`, `(f)+G-Z` is effective, so `deg Z<=deg G` and the outer weight is at least `7,340,032`.
The affine truth-table map is binary linear and injective; every nonzero nonconstant affine Boolean function is balanced.
Concatenation multiplies the dimension by eight and the outer weight lower bound by 64. Appending `16,384` zeros gives exact length `2^30`.
proof_steps.statement: The final code has exact dimension `3,915,368` and minimum distance at least `469,762,048`.

proof_steps.proof: Exact cross-multiplication gives numerator `10,264`, reducing the rate excess to `1,283/2,013,265,920>0`.
